original_question: Can SL(n, C) be holomorphically immersed in C^n −1 . [Cannot be done algebraically, true if n=2]
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the manifold SL(n,C), the analytic property being asked for (holomorphic immersion), and the paper's two bracketed side remarks: that the corresponding algebraic immersion is impossible and that the answer is known to be yes for n=2.
missing_details: The target space should be written as C^(n^2-1), not C^(n-1); your draft appears to have lost the square in the exponent.
The quantifier in n should be made explicit: the problem is asking for the general n-case, not just one fixed n.
To make the question stand-alone, SL(n,C) should be identified as the complex special linear group.
The intended target is complex Euclidean space of the same complex dimension as SL(n,C).
The question is purely holomorphic/complex-analytic; the bracketed algebraic remark is background, not an added hypothesis.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 2, does the complex special linear group SL(n,C) admit a holomorphic immersion into C^(n^2-1)?
justification: This is the Narasimhan problem listed as Problem 9.5.2 in the subsection 'Stein manifolds'. The ar5iv HTML extraction suppresses the displayed formulas in Problems 9.5.1-9.5.4, but Problem 9.5.2 still preserves the exact identifying note '[Cannot be done algebraically, true if n=2]'. That, together with the neighboring same-dimension immersion question in Problem 9.5.1 and the standard complex dimension of SL(n,C), pins down the intended formulation as the equal-dimension immersion problem for SL(n,C), namely immersion into C^(n^2-1). So your draft is very close in substance, but it needs the corrected exponent and an explicit quantifier in n to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
